note.explanation: Temperature tells how hot or cold a body is. Heat is energy transferred between bodies because they have different temperatures. A body has internal energy, not heat stored inside it.
examples: A spoon becomes hot when left in hotter water: thermal energy transfers from the water to the spoon.
When you touch a cold surface, energy transfers from your warmer hand to the surface.
note.checkAnswer: Thermal energy flows from the body at higher temperature to the body at lower temperature.
note.simple: Temperature tells how hot or cold something is. Heat is energy moving from a hotter object to a colder one.
note.checkQuestion: Which way does thermal energy flow when two bodies have different temperatures?
note.title: Temperature, Heat and Internal Energy
steps: Compare the temperatures of the two bodies.
Thermal energy transfers from the body at higher temperature to the body at lower temperature.
The energy transferred is called heat.
The sum of the molecules' kinetic and potential energies is the body's internal energy.
note.answer: Heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body because of a temperature difference.

rationales: Internal energy includes molecular potential energy as well as kinetic energy.

examTips: Expect short-answer questions asking for the definitions of temperature and heat; use the textbook wording accurately.
A question may ask what determines the direction of heat flow. State both the cause (temperature difference) and the direction (higher temperature to lower temperature).
For a distinction question, do not call heat energy contained in a body: heat is in transit, while internal energy is the sum of molecular kinetic and potential energies.
In explanation questions about heating, link the steps: molecular motion becomes more vigorous, internal energy increases, and temperature rises.

Include both energy transfer and the temperature difference between the bodies.

steps.why: The activity asks whether the spoon heats up when placed in hotter water.
steps.text: Put the spoon in the hot water and stir it.

steps.why: A spoon becoming hotter shows that energy has transferred to it.
steps.text: The spoon gets hotter, including its other end.

steps.why: The water is at a higher temperature than the spoon, so energy transfers from the water to the spoon.
steps.text: Heat is transferred from the hot water to the spoon because the temperature of the water was higher than that of the spoon.

example.question: Does the other end of the spoon also become hot?
example.answer: Yes. The spoon gets hotter because heat is transferred from the hotter water to the spoon.

explain.title: Temperature
explain.body: Temperature of a body is defined as degree of its hotness or coldness. Temperature also determines the direction in which thermal energy flows.

explain.title: Heat
explain.body: Heat is the energy which is transferred from one object to another due to difference of temperature between the two bodies. It is energy in transit, not something a body contains.

explain.title: Internal energy
explain.body: The sum of kinetic and potential energies of the molecules of an object is called its internal energy. Molecules have kinetic energy because they move and potential energy because attractive forces act between them.

explain.title: Heating a substance
explain.body: When a substance is heated, its molecular motion becomes more vigorous and its internal energy increases. As a result, its temperature rises.

mistakes: Writing that a body contains heat; the textbook says that a substance contains internal energy.
Defining heat without mentioning energy transfer due to a temperature difference.
Reversing the direction of heat flow: thermal energy transfers from higher temperature to lower temperature.
Defining internal energy as kinetic energy alone and forgetting the molecules' potential energy.
